title: Fiber Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/hello", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Hello, Asha!") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: A Fiber handler returns an error value. SendString writes the response text. Open GET /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The matching handler receives a Fiber v2 context. Returning SendString returns any writing error too. Return the error from response-writing methods.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/book", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"title": "Moon Trip"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: JSON writes an object as JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: JSON serialises the map as a response object. Use the Fiber v2 context pointer shown in this course.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/hello/:name", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Hi, " + c.Params("name") + "!") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Params reads a named path part. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Params reads the name segment Ravi, which is joined into a greeting. Path parameters start as text.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/page", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"page": c.Query("n", "1")}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Query reads a query value and can take a default. Open GET /page. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Query has no n input, so it returns the default string 1. A query value remains text until you parse it.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/double/:n", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { n, err := c.ParamsInt("n"); if err != nil { return c.Status(400).SendString("Use a whole number") }; return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"answer": n * 2}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: ParamsInt parses a route value as an integer. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: ParamsInt parses 4 successfully. The handler doubles the integer and returns JSON. Check the error before using the parsed number.

questions.question: BodyParser fills a struct from the request body. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: BodyParser fills the struct by pointer. The nonempty Title check succeeds before the 201 reply. Parsing does not replace checks for a useful field value.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
api := app.Group("/api")
api.Get("/books", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON([]string{"Moon Trip"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Group adds a shared path prefix. Open GET /api/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The group combines /api with /books for its final route. Request the group prefix as well as the inner path.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Use(func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { c.Locals("school", "Oak School"); return c.Next() })
app.Get("/school", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString(c.Locals("school").(string)) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Locals stores a value for the current request. A middleware can set it before a route reads it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The middleware stores a per-request local and calls Next. The route reads it as a string. Check a value type if it may come from a different source.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/note", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { c.Set("Cache-Control", "no-store"); return c.SendString("Practice note") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Set adds a response header. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Set adds Cache-Control before SendString writes the response. Set headers before sending the body.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/start", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Redirect("/hello", 302) })
app.Get("/hello", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Welcome") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Redirect sends a location and status. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Redirect writes a 302 response with /hello as its location. A redirect requires another client request.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/missing", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Status(404).JSON(fiber.Map{"error": "Book not found"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: Status selects a code before a body is sent. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Status changes the response code before JSON writes the error body. A helpful error body should keep the correct error status.

questions.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Home") })
app.Use(func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Status(404).SendString("Page not found") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}
questions.question: A final Use handler can reply when no earlier route handled the request. Open GET /unknown. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: No earlier route handles /unknown, so the last middleware returns a 404 text response. Put a catch-all handler after the real routes.
